issues.title: [1.21.1] Compatibility crash: Waystones onLoad in Sable stack; initiating action unconfirmed

labels.name: Minecraft 1.21.1
labels.description: Issues occurring in Minecraft 1.21.1

issues.body:
### Clarification from the affected player

The affected player has clarified that the incident involved a portal from Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks (installed version 1.21.1-3.16.3). The precise spell/item name and whether the crash followed creating, entering, or leaving the portal are not yet confirmed. This is a player report, not a controlled reproduction. The portal is the reported gameplay context; no direct portal-to-crash call chain has been established.

Waystones onLoad/sync is confirmed in the immediate exception stack. This does NOT establish that the player interacted with a waystone, or that Waystones initiated the incident. Iron's Spellbooks appears in the Level mixin list, but that alone does not establish causation either. A preceding action could potentially have caused chunk/block-entity loading; this is an unverified hypothesis. Root cause and which mod needs a fix remain undetermined.

### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Mod Loader

NeoForge 21.1.250 (dedicated server)

### Describe the Issue

Our server crashed while a Waystones block entity was loading, with `UnsupportedOperationException: Cannot change blocks in nonexistent plot holder` thrown by Sable's block-change hook.

The observed call chain is:

`WaystoneBlockEntityBase.onLoad:152 → BalmBlockEntity.sync:172 → ServerChunkCache.blockChanged → Sable blockChanged injection`

The world saved during shutdown, but the JVM remained alive with a stuck thread warning and no game/RCON listeners. Restarting the unchanged server restored startup and ticking.

I have also reported the crash to Sable: https://github.com/ryanhcode/sable/issues/1635

I understand the exception is thrown inside Sable, so this is a compatibility report rather than a claim that Waystones is at fault. Could you advise whether Waystones onLoad/sync needs any integration guard, or whether an existing addon/version is the intended solution for this case?

I found https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/issues/1153 and https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/issues/1229. Those concern teleport positioning/freezes and mention the Waystones: Sable addon. We have not tested that addon or established that it fixes this specific onLoad crash.

### Environment

- Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.250, dedicated server
- Sable 2.0.5
- Waystones 21.1.42, Balm 21.0.65
- Create 6.0.10, Create Aeronautics 1.3.2
- Sable / Stuff & Additions compatibility addon: sable_sa_compat 1.0.4
- Windows 11 amd64, Java 23.0.2
- This is a large modpack. Sinytra Connector 2.0.0-beta.17+1.21.1 is installed.

### Reproduction status

Observed once on the running server on October 17, 2026 (server local time, UTC-7). We do not know the exact player action, whether the affected waystone was on a sublevel, or whether a sublevel had just been removed. No minimal mod set, test without Connector, or controlled reproduction has been completed. The stack trace identifies the call chain, but does not establish which mod should fix it.

### Logs

Sanitized log excerpt, including the exception chain and shutdown outcome (not the full crash report): https://mclo.gs/I8xbQW0

The original crash report is retained privately; server paths and player details are not published.

issues.title: Better resource pack support for runes

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Right now all waystones share the same `waystone_runes` model, and tinting is hardcoded based on waystone style. 
This limits resource packs to 1) have all waystone styles share the same shape, and 2) have to adapt to the predefined tinting.

It would be better if each type had its own runes model (that can just use the shared one as parent) - that way they can be overridden individually. There should also be a way to define the tint color in the resource pack.

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.20.1

### Mod Loader

Forge

### Describe the Issue

After updating Waystones from 14.1.20 to 14.1.21, Mekanism's gas tag `mekanism:water_vapor` ends up empty on world load, breaking the mekanism:injecting/coral/brain_coral_fan recipe (Injection Chamber).

Log errors right after "Server resource reload complete!":
[Server thread/ERROR]: Incomplete recipe detected: mekanism:injecting/coral/brain_coral_fan
[Server thread/ERROR]: Empty tag: TagKey[mekanism:gas / mekanism:water_vapor]

In-game chat also shows:
[Mekanism] Broken tags in Mekanism recipes detected, please check server logs for details.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Install Waystones 14.1.21 alongside Mekanism 10.4.16.80 on Forge 47.4.18 / MC 1.20.1.
2. Launch the world.
3. Observe the errors above in the log and the chat warning.

Expected behavior:
The mekanism:water_vapor gas tag should still contain mekanism:water_vapor after loading, as it did on Waystones 14.1.20.

Testing done:
Confirmed by disabling mods one at a time. Only removing Waystones makes the error disappear; other mods updated in the same session (JourneyMap, Sophisticated Backpacks) were ruled out this way. Re-adding the tag manually via a KubeJS script also resolves the issue without needing to downgrade Waystones, confirming the tag itself is the point of failure:

ServerEvents.tags('mekanism:gas', event => {
    event.add('mekanism:water_vapor', 'mekanism:water_vapor')
})

### Logs

I also turn the server off when we're not playing, plus with the various security measures I have taken, it can't have been anyone else joining the server. issues.title: Gametime-based block rendering becomes choppy

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: NeoForge
labels.description: Issues occurring on the NeoForge platform

labels.name: Minecraft 26.2
labels.description: Issues occurring in Minecraft 26.2

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

26.2

### Mod Loader

NeoForge

### Describe the Issue

The more time passes, the choppier the rendering of blocks which use gametime becomes.
We first noticed this happening when playing on a server with friends. It first became noticeable after about a week IRL of the server running non-stop, so it's not something that only happens after an absurdly long time.

At the moment, this affects:
- the items inside *Sharestones* rotating and bobbing up and down ([here](https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/26.2/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/client/render/SharestoneRenderer.java#L88-L89));
  - at gametime of 0: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/357119a0-066d-44e7-9871-c874441e7b90
  - at gametime of 10 IRL days: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6101b00e-7f43-4b56-a4d4-6cf79a86b948
- *Fleeting Memorials* bobbing up and down ([here](https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/26.2/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/client/render/FleetingMemorialRenderer.java#L81)).
  - at gametime of 10 IRL days: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41cf649a-0838-4ffc-862b-0090c586d301

I believe this is caused by casting the gametime, which is a `long`, directly to a `float`. Floating-point numbers do not have adequate precision to store a large gametime, but they do not need to do so in the first place - the effects gametime is used for are cyclical. If using gametime, this can potentially be fixed by first `%`-ing it with some smaller value, and only *then* doing float operations.

### Logs

Likely N/A, but: [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31656808/latest.log)

issues.title: [Bug] Warp modifiers do not apply when arriving at regular waystones

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Mod Loader

NeoForge

### Describe the Issue

# [Bug] Warp modifiers do not apply when arriving at regular waystones

### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Mod Loader

NeoForge

### Mod Loader Version

21.1.235

### Mod Version

21.1.41

### Balm Version

21.0.65

### Describe the Issue

Warp modifier items placed in a regular waystone do not apply their effects to entities arriving at that waystone.

I tested this with 32 Blaze Powder in the modifier inventory of the destination waystone. `enableModifiers` was enabled, but arriving at that waystone did not set the player on fire.

The items were placed in the destination waystone, not the source waystone.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Place and activate two regular waystones, A and B.
2. Make sure `enableModifiers` is set to `true`.
3. Open the modifier inventory of waystone B.
4. Put 32 Blaze Powder into one of its modifier slots.
5. Use waystone A to teleport to waystone B.
6. Observe that the player is not set on fire.

### Expected Behavior

The player should be set on fire for approximately 32 seconds after arriving at waystone B.

### Actual Behavior

No modifier effect is applied.

### Possible Cause

This appears to be caused by the destination block entity being looked up at the entity's arrival position instead of at the target waystone's position.

In `WaystoneTeleportManager`, the target block entity is obtained using:

```java
final var targetPos = BlockPos.containing(destination.location());
BlockEntity targetTileEntity = targetLevel.getBlockEntity(targetPos);
```

Regular waystones offset their teleport destination to an adjacent block based on the waystone's facing direction. Therefore, `targetPos` normally points to the air block in front of the waystone rather than the waystone itself.

As a result, this check fails for regular waystones:

```java
if (context.appliesModifiers()
        && targetTileEntity instanceof WaystoneBlockEntityBase waystoneBlockEntity) {
    teleportedEntities.forEach(waystoneBlockEntity::applyModifierEffects);
}
```

Relevant code:

- Teleport completion and modifier lookup:  
  https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/1.21.1/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/WaystoneTeleportManager.java#L151-L169
- Regular waystone destination offset:  
  https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/1.21.1/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/WaystoneTeleportManager.java#L243-L281

A possible fix would be to look up the modifier container using the actual target waystone position, for example:

```java
BlockEntity targetWaystoneBlockEntity = targetLevel.getBlockEntity(
        context.getTargetWaystone().getPos()
);
```

and use that block entity when applying modifiers.

The affected code is in the common module, so this may not be specific to NeoForge.

### Affected Versions / Cross-Version Source Comparison

This does not appear to be exclusive to Minecraft 1.21.1 or NeoForge. A comparison of the current official source branches shows the following:

| Minecraft versions | Implementation and likely impact |
| --- | --- |
| 1.19.2–1.20.6 | Modifier effects were primarily implemented in `WarpPlateBlockEntity`. Regular waystones did not yet use the same generalized modifier mechanism, so this specific regular-waystone lookup issue does not apply in the same way. |
| 1.21.1 | The regular-waystone modifier implementation looks up the block entity at the entity's arrival position, causing this issue. |
| 1.21.3–1.21.11 | The same arrival-position block entity lookup is still present, so regular waystones appear to be affected there as well. |
| 26.1–26.3 | Modifier effects were refactored into the rules system, but the block entity passed to `afterWarpEffects` is still obtained from the arrival position. The issue therefore appears to remain. |

Examples from the official repository:

- Minecraft 1.20.6, modifiers implemented in `WarpPlateBlockEntity`:  
  https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/1.20.6/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/block/entity/WarpPlateBlockEntity.java
- Minecraft 1.21.11, still looking up the block entity at `destination.location()`:  
  https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/1.21.11/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/WaystoneTeleportManager.java
- Minecraft 26.2, the rules implementation still receives the block entity found at the arrival position:  
  https://github.com/TwelveIterations/Waystones/blob/26.2/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/WaystoneTeleportManager.java

These additional versions were identified through source comparison and were not all reproduced in-game. Since the affected lookup is in the `common` module, the issue is likely shared by NeoForge, Forge, and Fabric.

issues.title: [Feature] Optional Redstone Control for Warp Plates

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Description
I would like to request an optional redstone control feature for the Warp Plate (warp_plate). Currently, the plate teleports any entity that steps onto it instantly. I propose adding a toggleable setting (e.g., via the plate’s GUI) that switches its activation mode from “always on” to “redstone‑controlled”.

Suggested Implementation
Add a new button or slider in the Warp Plate’s GUI, labelled something like “Activation Mode” with two options:

Instant / Always Active (current behaviour)

Redstone Required (plate only activates when powered by redstone signal)

When set to redstone mode, the plate should:

Visually indicate its powered state (e.g., change particle colour or emit a glow when active).

Only teleport entities if it receives a redstone signal (strength ≥ 1) at the moment of activation.

Optionally, respect the existing cooldown and delay settings even in redstone mode.

Why This Would Be Useful
Better integration with automation – players could build sequenced teleportation networks, triggered by pressure plates, timers, or logic circuits.

Safety – prevents accidental teleportation when walking near the plate, especially in tight bases.

Map‑making / adventure packs – allows designers to create puzzle or timed‑teleport mechanics without external mods.

Additional Considerations
The default should remain “Always Active” to avoid breaking existing builds.

If possible, also expose the mode via the config file or datapack for server‑wide defaults.

Thank you for considering this suggestion! I really enjoy the mod and this small addition would open up many new creative possibilities.

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Mod Loader

Fabric (Loader 0.19.3)

### Mod Version

21.1.36+fabric-1.21.1 (Balm 21.0.62)

### Describe the Issue

On a dedicated multiplayer server, two players riding the **same vanilla boat** teleport via a waystone. Both players are teleported correctly, but the boat desyncs: the **driver** (the one who activated the waystone) no longer sees the boat, while the **passenger** still sees it. Appears to be the same client-side entity desync as #402 / #718 (entity teleports but fails to render on one client).

**Reproduction:**
1. Player A (driver) + Player B (passenger) in one vanilla boat.
2. Player A activates a waystone and teleports.
3. Both arrive; Player A's client no longer renders the boat, Player B still sees it.

Consistent. No crash — purely a visual/entity desync, nothing logged.

### Performance/other mods

Yes — this is a large Cobblemon modpack (Cobbleverse) including Sodium, Lithium, C2ME, EntityCulling and ModernFix, so a client render/culling interaction can't be fully ruled out.

### Minecraft Version

### Describe the Issue

Describe the Issue
Using a Warp Stone that was previously taken from an unbuilt Warp Plate causes the client to crash when inserted into a newly placed Warp Plate and used.

Crash points to Waystones:

```java
java.lang.ClassCastException: class net.minecraft.client.player.LocalPlayer cannot be cast to class net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer (net.minecraft.client.player.LocalPlayer and net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer are in unnamed module of loader 'knot' @46d56d67)
	at knot//net.blay09.mods.waystones.block.entity.WaystoneBlockEntityBase.getSettingsMenuProvider(WaystoneBlockEntityBase.java:279)
	at knot//net.blay09.mods.waystones.block.WarpPlateBlock.useWithoutItem(WarpPlateBlock.java:183)
```

Steps to reproduce

1. Place two Warp Plates.
2. Insert Warp Stones into them.
3. Unbuild/remove one Warp Plate.
4. Take the Warp Stone from the removed Warp Plate.
5. Place a new Warp Plate.
6. Insert the Warp Stone from the old Warp Plate into the new one.
7. Use the new Warp Plate.
8. The game crashes.

Expected behavior
The reused Warp Stone should work normally in the new Warp Plate, or the Warp Plate should safely reject/reset invalid old data without crashing.

Actual behavior
The client crashes when using the new Warp Plate with the reused Warp Stone.

Environment

issues.title: Configuration setting for Waystone harvest level / mining tier

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Currently, Waystones are relatively easy to break and move in survival mode. While there is a `restrictToCreative` setting, there is no middle ground for modpack authors who want to gate Waystone relocation behind specific progression tiers (e.g., requiring a Netherite pickaxe to move a Waystone).

Attempting to change this via data packs or script engines (like KubeJS) can be inconsistent due to how Block Entities handle drops and how different Minecraft versions map tool tiers.

I would like to see a new entry in the `waystones-common.toml` (or server config) that allows us to define the required harvest level for Waystones.

Ideally, it would look something like this:

```
# The harvest level required to break and drop a waystone. 
# 0=Wood, 1=Stone, 2=Iron, 3=Diamond, 4=Netherite
harvestLevel = 4
```

This would be incredibly helpful for "Expert" style modpacks where exploration and fast travel are intended to be late-game rewards.

```
#If enabled, only creative players can place, edit or break waystones. This does NOT disable the crafting recipe.
	restrictToCreative = true

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.1 (LTS)

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Describe the Issue

`getWaystone` has several paths that call `sync` as part of lazy-initialization, but this method is also called from within block updates (i.e. within sync() itself), meaning it will schedule an update while the update is already happening.

This results in a chunk becoming desynced when spawning a waystone using `setblock`.

Coupled with C2ME it also results in a crash.

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.10

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Describe the Issue

Place five Warp Plates.

1. Attune the first four Warp Plates to the fifth Warp Plate.
2. Insert one Nether Quartz modifier into each Warp Plate. (The same issue occurs if only the fifth Warp Plate has Nether Quartz or all Warp Plates have Nether Quartz.)
3. Drop items repeatedly onto the fifth Warp Plate.

Expected Behavior:
Items should be distributed to the linked Warp Plates in a predictable round-robin order (Plate 1 → Plate 2 → Plate 3 → Plate 4 → repeat).

Actual Behavior:
Items are teleported to the linked Warp Plates in random order, with no visible round-robin sequence.

### Logs

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23467019/latest.log)

I am including the latest.log even though it does not contain any related errors or warnings to the Bug.

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Playing in multiplayer, people will still call their waystones "Home" etc.

This means if you activate their waystones, you end up with many different "Home" waystones unless everyone gets the memo to give more descriptive names.

Players should be able to assign an alias to a waystone they activated, i.e. being able to rename it for themselves only.

Perhaps certain words could trigger automatic aliases upon activation (e.g. when activating a "Home", the alias starts out as "<Owner>'s Home".

Waystones create waypoints in Journeymap. However, no group is created in the waypoint manager. This makes it hard to disable all waystone waypoints. This is caused by something that changed in journeymap-neoforge-1.21.1-6.0.0-beta.48.jar. Mysticdrew of the Journeymap mod says that something needs to be updated in waystones mod.

Unfortunately, I can't find any instructions in the [changelog](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/journeymap/files/6635000/changelog).

### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Mod Loader

NeoForge

### Describe the Issue

Issue starting yesterday where chunks wouldn't generate/render when exploring new areas. Tried generating a new world and it failed at 0%.

Spent a couple hours enabling/disabling various mods, found I was able to get worlds to generate and the chunks in my SP world to start appearing again with Waystones disabled.

I haven't tested with JUST waystones installed, but I disabled all content mods and only left performance mods enabled and still got the crash. It could be conflicting with one of those, but I'm not exactly sure and I'm not experienced enough to figure it out.

I do know that downgrading to the previous version of Waystones has fixed the issue for me.

issues.body: ### Minecraft Version Other (specify below) ### Mod Loader Fabric ### Describe the Issue Hello! I have a server where we use the Waystones mod and its inventory button as one of the main ways to move around the map intradimensionally. We noticed that the inventory button doesn't work in the Nether, so we can't select any waystones in the Nether with it. However, interacting with waystones directly work as expected. I was able to repro on a server with the Waystones mod + dependencies with 1 active waystone in the Overworld and 1 active waystone in the Nether. MC 1.21.5 Fabric Loader 0.16.14 Waystones 21.5.8 The warp requirement to disable interdimensional travel prevents all teleports to waystones when inside the Nether. The inventory button is greyed out, even though there is an active waystone in the Nether. `"[is_interdimensional] refuse(Cannot teleport to another dimension.)"` The problem is the same when I tried using more granular warp requirements, but it looks like the inventory button assumes we're trying to teleport to the Overworld and blocks usage, even though there is an active waystone in the Nether. ``` "[source_is_dimension(minecraft:overworld), target_is_dimension(minecraft:the_nether)] refuse(You cannot warp to the Nether from the Overworld.)", "[source_is_dimension(minecraft:the_nether), target_is_dimension(minecraft:overworld)] refuse(You cannot warp to the Overworld from the Nether.)" ``` The inventory button works as expected in the Overworld. Moving the modifiers and conditions to the top of the `warpRequirements` list, to the bottom, or just isolating them resulted in the same issue. I didn't test other warp requirement setups, waystone blocks, or dimensions. ### Logs https://mclo.gs/OBUcsWl https://mclo.gs/eYXyxhz

issues.title: Support more complex warp requirements as data packs

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Currently warp requirements are still limited by the fact that they use a custom syntax designed for simple inline strings. For example, it would get fairly difficult to express NBT data.

It would be nice if **alongside the existing system**, the config option could also reference a rule from a data pack, which could then be defined as regular json. In the background we could convert any inline rules to the json-based structured data as well so that we'd continue to have just one single representation in code.

A datapack defining custom rules would only provide them for optional use, the source of truth on which rules should apply would still be the config option, e.g.

```toml
warpRequirements = ["import(mydatapack:mycustomrule)"]
```

In Unbreakables we achieve a similar thing through a "rulesets" config option seperate to "rules", but since order matters in Waystones a custom `import()` rule works better here. 

I do not want to get rid of the custom format because it has shown itself to be fairly intuitive and can easily be embedded in the existing config file to cover the majority of use cases. However, since the same system is also in use by Unbreakables, perhaps it could be extracted into a lightweight Jar-in-Jar dependency (I don't believe it has a place in Balm).

issues.body:
I'm a DEV of **Every Compat (Stone Zone)**. it's possible to support your mod BUT the issue is the ID. 

I know it's not possible for you to change the Ids like `waystone` to `stone_brick_waystone` or `stone_waystone`. We both know changing the Id could break the world or cause headache for people who use your mod in servers. 

but there is one simple solution: Added `blackstone_waystone`, the ID must be like that way. So i can support your mod with variant StoneTypes (A new stone sets added by other mods) 

I've looked at your source code for 1.21.1 and it already has `blackstone_waystone` and `end_stone_waystone`, I should have no problem supporting your mod for 1.21.1. Just 1.20.1 need to be updated to have these blocks included. 

You can let me know if you have updated the 1.20.1 to have these blocks or decide to not bother with 1.20.1

issues.body:
Hi, recently you made an internal change to only create sharestones for specific (the vanilla) dyes, instead of just any present DyeColor values.
I made a mod ("dye the world") a few months back that adds support between the mod "dye depot" and various other mods, including this one. It adds models and data for sharestones with that mods dyes.

While your change makes sense and is a lot cleaner, this of course does not work now anymore, since these blocks do not get created anymore. I have to take a closer look at the code again, but I was wondering if to make it work again, I would need an API on waystones side to allow more colors, which I could call from my compat mod?

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.5

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Describe the Issue

Honestly, I'm not even sure they are supposed to exist at the moment. If not, then this is more of a feature request. This is my first real playthrough with this mod.

But since I found both code that looks like it might be for a tooltip (`appendHoverText` in BoundScrollItem) and old issues with screenshots of tooltip on a Bound Scroll ... here i am.

What items are missing tooltips? As far as i can tell all of them.
You can only tell a Waystone's name by placing it down (and see that it is named because it doesn't stack).
Bound Scrolls don't tell you where it is bound to. Neither do Return Scrolls tell you their destinations.

Only the Blank/Unbound Scroll has a tooltip about what to do with it.
Nothing else does, aside from Durability on Warp Stones.

I've confirmed that this happens with only (also the newest) Waystones (Fabric) installed, so it's unlikely to be a interfering mod.

### Logs

Both are missing tooltips. Only the more modded one shows any error mentioning Waystones:
`java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.util.UUID.toString()" because "waystoneUid" is null`
Here i connect to a fabric server.
[From my more modded instance.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20242954/From.my.more.modded.instance.log)

Tested in Singleplayer. Nothing in it really.
[From the only Waystones instance.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20243001/From.the.only.Waystones.instance.log)

Tried to see if there is already an issue for it but didn't find any about tooltips missing. Sorry if I overlooked them.
And thanks for read/looking into this.

### Minecraft Version

1.21.1 (LTS)

### Mod Loader

NeoForge

### Describe the Issue

`RequirementModifierParser` cant prase a requirement from other mods due to `Pattern.compile("(\\w+)\\((.*?)\\)");` cant match `:`

see   https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/f20d025d72480d05947e4ba9de8d6ea6340689d0/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/requirement/RequirementModifierParser.java#L57

https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/f20d025d72480d05947e4ba9de8d6ea6340689d0/common/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/requirement/RequirementModifierParser.java#L66

change it to `Pattern.compile("([\\w:]+)\\((.*?)\\)");` could work

issues.title: Feature Request: Add “NON_SEATED” Option for Pet Teleportation

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

labels.name: Needs Discussion
labels.description: This may be considered in the future and I'm looking for more opinions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
I'd like to request an additional configuration option for pet teleportation behavior.  
Currently, the `transportPets` setting supports `ENABLED`, `SAME_DIMENSION`, and `DISABLED`. However, there's no way to distinguish between **sitting** and **standing** pets.

## Proposal
Introduce a new option—`NON_SEATED`—for `transportPets`. This would teleport **only standing pets**, ignoring any pets that are sitting.

## Why this matters
- In vanilla Minecraft, sitting pets are used to indicate “stay here.” Teleporting them anyway goes against expected behavior.  
- Players may accidentally teleport their entire pet collection—dogs, cats, parrots, etc.—to dangerous dimensions like the Nether, simply by forgetting they were nearby.  
- It would offer much-needed control and prevent accidents without requiring leads or disabling pet transport entirely.

## Suggested Config Snippet
```
# Waystones Teleportation Settings
# Set to ENABLED to have nearby pets teleport with you.
# Set to SAME_DIMENSION to have nearby pets teleport only when not changing dimensions.
# Set to DISABLED to disable pet teleportation.
# **NEW**: Set to NON_SEATED to teleport only standing (non-sitting) pets.
transportPets = "NON_SEATED"```
```


I'm not sure how difficult this change would be to implement, but I believe it would be a valuable quality-of-life improvement. Thanks for considering!

issues.title: [Suggestion / Request] Instead of waystones menu, use a map to select waystone points

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

labels.name: Needs Discussion
labels.description: This may be considered in the future and I'm looking for more opinions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
I've been using Waystones on a custom modded server for a long time. The modpack uses Xaero's map mods and integrations between waystones and the map. Which already helps a lot to know which waystone is where.

But whilst playing other video games like newer 3D Legend of Zelda games, Or like how Terraria functions with Pylons. I've realized that instead of the cluttered waystone select UI screen, it would make things much easier and more convenient if there was an option to just open up the world map when interacting with a waystone. And when you open the world map via waystone or nearby one activated one, it enables the option to travel to any waystone point on the map.

You can still show the XP cost when hovering over the waystone points on the map.

So in a nutshell my request is:
- right clicking on a waystone opens up the world map
- when near a waystone, clicking on waystone waypoints on the world map allows you to teleport there, like you normally would trough a waystone UI

Not sure if this is doable, since it would most likely need another world map mod to work with, but I just wanted to share this suggestion. Either way, thank you for the amazing mod and the continuous support of it!

issues.title: Add a fature to configure mod with permissions plugins/mods

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Sometimes it's important as admin to have a feature to give some permisson to some player or do something with waypoint.

For example if some player left a server and u want to change a waystone, the only way for you as an admin have to achieve that is  to break the waypoint and place it again with your configuration. And if the player will return one day the waystone will be missing for them. Moreover all players will have to add this waypoint again after this process.
If some player put a waystone with a bad name I just want to rename it, not to break. 
It looks like the case for the permisson system that exists since craftbukket and still used by the most admins.

The same goes and for /waystone commands. I can find myself in need to give a permission to someone to use a command. Or frobid from using it.

### Minecraft Version

Other (specify below)

### Mod Loader

Forge

### Mod Version

11.4.2

### Describe the Issue


**An exploit allows duplicating items using the Warp Plate GUI. 
My game version is 1.19.2, but this exploit should theoretically work in most versions. 
Steps to reproduce:**

- One player opens the Warp Plate GUI and places the item they want to duplicate inside, without closing the GUI.
- Another player (or a mod with fake player functionality) breaks the Warp Plate block.
- The item inside the Warp Plate drops on the ground, but the first player's GUI remains open.
- The first player can retrieve the item from the GUI, effectively duplicating it.

issues.title: Request: Death scroll/stone that allows a player to warp to their death location

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
It'd be super nice to have items that allow a player to warp to the location of their last death, essentially as a more balanced alternative to things like `/back`.

Since this shouldn't be too hard, I'm happy to implement it myself.

Here's what I'm currently thinking (item names should probably be changed):

---

### Death Scroll

Recipe: Same as return scroll but with 3 bones above (or maybe 2 bones and a cobweb?).

Usage:
- Using the scroll teleports the player to their most recent death location, if one exists, after a short windup time.


### Death Stone

Recipe: Same as warp stone but with soul lanterns instead of the amethyst (replacing the emerald with a totem could be thematically nicer, but I think it's too expensive).

Usage:
- Using the stone teleports the player to their most recent death location, if one exists, after a short windup time.

---

Does this sound good?

issues.title: Request: Player-bound Scrolls

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Waystones has been my favorite teleportation based mod for a long time now. I love the way that it has replaced command-based teleport functions like Homes or Warps with something that has more limitations and physical items within the world. 

I wondered if you would consider adding Player-bound scrolls as a one-time-use tp to player function? They would save what player they are bound to similarly to the current bound scrolls, and upon use, teleport you to that specific player. 

I understand this may be outside the scope of the mod, but it felt like something that is just in-line enough with the concept to merit suggesting. They could even be a toggle-able feature in the config to not upset balance for servers that would prefer to not use them.

Thanks in advance!

issues.body: there currently isn't a way to change within which biomes the naturally generating waystones can generate. as they spawn exclusively within vanilla biomes, i'm pretty sure that internally this mod uses a tag to pick the biomes, but the tag is presumably one that already exists, such as #minecraft:is_jungle for example (there are worldgen tags too, but as far as i know they aren't used for this). it'd be annoying to have to change a vanilla tag just for this mod, so i propose the creation and use of tags that are specifically created by the mod (a tag that would define the biomes within which the sandy waystones spawn could be named #waystones:sandy_waystone_spawns for example). this hand over the much needed and appreciated control over this feature to modpack makers such as myself!

A somewhat frequent report with Waystones is that servers are experiencing lagspikes or clients are falling through the ground on teleports.

Since nowadays chunk loading does support CompletableFuture to some extent, it might be time to look into whether the teleport's chunk load could be initiated off the main thread.

Some things to watch out for:
- [x] what if player moves away
- [x] what if the waystone is broken
- [x] what if player drops the stone or scroll
- [x] what if player uses the stone or scroll again
- [x] what if player dies
- [x] what if leashed entities or pets change

### Describe the Issue

The issue is discussed in https://github.com/celsiusqc/TowersOfTheWildModded/issues/17

Waystones can sometimes (seemingly randomly) prevent the top of the towers in Towers of The Wild - modded to generate. The top part containing the waystone is a separate structure from the tower part. This only happens with Waystones mod enabled.

After some research by SettingDust, it seems there's some issue in the waystones code causing this. They say in the ticket linked above:

> https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/1.20.1/shared/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/mixin/SinglePoolElementMixin.java#L51
>
> after research. Waystone will block the generating since https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/1.20.1/shared/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/mixin/SinglePoolElementMixin.java#L34 the path containing the string.
>
> It's for only one in every village from the comment. But the logic is terrible
>
> Need to blocking the mixin injecting the wayston into village with https://github.com/Bawnorton/MixinSquared
> And reinject the waystone element into the pool with https://modrinth.com/mod/lithostitched.
> Maybe I'll create a standalone mod for that XD

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
- Remove the slot interfaces
- Attuned Shard creation happens in world, where the shard will pop out of the center of a warp plate
- Insert an attuned shard into the warp plate's in-world slot by right click to set the target
- Insert a crumbling shard into the warp plate's in-world slot by right click to set a one-time target (this means warp plates with a permanent target and a temporary target will no longer be possible)
- Craft a Dormant Shard and insert it to attune it to that warp plate (first will still be free)
- Craft a Bedrock Shard (or similar material) to lock a warp plate into being a target only
- Remove Landing Plates in favor of locked warp plates

- _(maybe later) New Warp Seal item that holds the original slot interface, supports the item effect modifiers and can be used to add additional warp targets, applicable to waystones, sharestones and warp plates and effective on departures_

issues.title: Replace dimensionalWarp, dimensionalWarpAllowList and dimensionalWarpDenyList with more granular options

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Since Waystones grew, having only "ALLOW", "GLOBAL_ONLY" and "DENY" is no longer flexible enough. There are use cases where you would want only sharestones to allow dimensional teleport, or only warp plates, or only the inventory button, or only players who have unlocked a certain advancement, ...

The new cost modifier system can represent these cases pretty well if a "refuse()" option is added. Might even rename it something like "warpConfig" to better fit for cases where it's not strictly a "cost". Would also need to support parameters in conditions (which is good to have anyways).

**Example for denyList:**
```toml
warpConfig = [
    "[is_dimension(the_nether)] refuse()"
    "[is_dimension(the_end)] refuse()"
]
```

**Example for allowList:**
```toml
warpConfig = [
    "[is_not_dimension(overworld), is_not_dimension(mining_world)] refuse()"
]
```

+ other conditions could be used (like `source_is_global` to replicate `GLOBAL_ONLY` from before).

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.20.1 (LTS)

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Mod Loader Version

0.15.2 with API 0.91

### Mod Version

14.1.2 / dev

### Balm Version

7.3.0-SNAPSHOT

### Describe the Issue

Any attempt at _using_ any warp plate fails with the `The shard inside this warp plate has lost its attunement` message
However, the shard's tooltip is not indicating the same. Nothing in particular in logs.

Ran into it on my dedicated server, and it took me a long time to reproduce on my machine: turns out this doesn't occur on fabric client runs with a local save, but does occur when both running the fabric-client and fabric-server.

Here's what I found:
 - stepping on the warp plate resolves a `WaystoneProxy` corresponding to the attuned shard in `WarpPlateBlockEntity#serverTick()`
 - the `WaystoneManager#get` call returns the static `clientStorageCopy` (the `server` parameter is `null`)
 - that particular manager is empty (`waystones.size() == 0`) on the server side
 - as a result the `isValid()` for the original proxy is `false` and an error is sent to the client directly (no attempt at teleporting)

I think the root cause is the fact that `WaystonesAPI#getBoundWaystone(ItemStack)` always uses `IAttunementItem#getWaystoneAttunedTo` with a `null` `server`... This is fine on client side, but leads to the bug on server side.

I can provide a small save/world to reproduce if needed.

Forge

### Mod Loader Version

43.2.21

### Mod Version

11.4.1

### Balm Version

4.6.0

### Describe the Issue

The minimum cost for XP for inverted distance calculations is improperly clamped. It has no minimum value because [L162-L166 of PlayerWaystoneManager](https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/fc93309faeb0627766addd7dc84c0a126d529374/shared/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/PlayerWaystoneManager.java#L162-L166),
```
xpLevelCost = Mth.clamp(Math.floor(dist / (float) WaystonesConfig.getActive().blocksPerXPLevel()), minimumXpCost, maximumXpCost);

if (WaystonesConfig.getActive().inverseXpCost()) {
    xpLevelCost = maximumXpCost - xpLevelCost;
}
```
only clamp to the minimum level to calculate the XP cost, and then inversion is done by subtracting from the maximum cost. This means that the XP cost is not clamped, and can reach zero as you approach the maximum configured distance.

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.20.x

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Mod Loader Version

0.14.22

### Mod Version

14.0.2

### Balm Version

7.1.4

### Describe the Issue

After trying to configure the xp costs of the various types of waystones/warp plates, I came to the conclusion that the math involved with max level cost, distance-per-level, and the individual multipliers seems to be wrong.

Specifically, I was trying to make Waystones cost 1 level per 1000 blocks, and Warp Plates cost 1 level per 100 blocks, both capping at 3 levels max.

However, the multiplier on cost seems to be applying *after* the level cap is applied; i tried to simply multiply Plate costs by 10, which I expected to be divided against the distance-per-level. Instead, setting 2 plates 1000 blocks apart costed 10 levels, while any less costed 0. Waystones were unaffected, being multiplied by 1.

Next, I tried setting distance-per-level to 100, and multiplying Waystone cost by 0.1. This worked for Plates, costing 1 level per 100 blocks distance up to 3. However, *this* solution caused all Waystones to be free; even at over 1000 blocks, where it should have been 1 level. (1000/100)*0.1 should be 1, after all.

The only conclusion I can reach from this is that multipliers and caps are being applied in the wrong order. The current formula seems to be

`COST = max(LEVELCAP, floor(DISTANCE/DISTANCE_PER_LEVEL) ) * MULTIPLIER`
where it should be something like
`COST = max(LEVELCAP, floor(DISTANCE/DISTANCE_PER_LEVEL * MULTIPLIER) )`

taking a look at the code myself, [i confirmed this to be the case.](https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/1.20.x/shared/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/PlayerWaystoneManager.java#L171) Multipliers are being added *after* level capping instead of during the distance/level calculation, causing them to behave unexpectedly.

issues.body:
It would be amazing if there was a config option to make it so waystone travel would cost and consume some item (say, emeralds) instead of experience. It would be ideal if the item could also be configurable so that a modpack could specify its currency item. 

I've seen others ask for this on the curseforge comments pages as well, so I know there is demand for it. This would be very useful for economy-based servers/modpacks as there is not a clean way to convert currency to experience that doesn't cause other issues gameplay-wise due to how experience works in the game. 

I thought about just making the scrolls/stones cost currency to craft, but the novelty of having to walk to a hub/location that contains a waystone before teleporting is too important to me to give up. issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

Forge

### Mod Loader Version

43.2.8

### Mod Version

11.4.0

### Balm Version

4.5.7

### Describe the Issue

:wave: A player came to me requesting help with their world never getting off the "Loading terrain" screen. By using a profiler I was able to track down that the server worker thread doing the chunk generation/loading gets stuck inside the `getShuffledTemplates` code, seemingly running `toString` forever, or at least enough times that it completely dominates the profiler's list of hot methods:

https://github.com/TwelveIterationMods/Waystones/blob/29a686bb9e294d2d7c9b67484e410fe668c0f01c/shared/src/main/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/mixin/JigsawPlacementMixin.java

I am aware that Waystones is a very popular mod used in other modpacks without issue so this is probably some other mod triggering the function to be run many times (possibly a structure mod). However, I would suggest that if possible the ID checks here should be cached, as needing to call `toString` on structure pieces over and over seems quite inefficient even if it doesn't cause issues in most cases. I'd also like to note that after removing Waystones the player's pack was able to load into the world without problems.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
The plan is have generated village waystones no longer drop as items when broken. Instead they will "shatter into pieces", leaving you only a cracked stone brick and some warp dust.

- Villages and village waystones are so easy to find that it's become the main means of farming waystones
- This counteracts the removal of xp costs for teleportation, shifting the balance™️ to acquisition costs since people will actually have to start crafting waystones (or run into the harder to find wild ones, if enabled).
- The `generatedWaystonesUnbreakable` config option will be removed
- There will likely be two new options `villageWaystonesShatterOnBreak` and `wildWaystonesShatterOnBreak` to control this behaviour

issues.title: [1.20] Replace Warp Stone cooldown with Durability

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

labels.name: Breaking Change
labels.description: This issue requires a breaking change to the API or ingame behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
The plan is to fully remove the warp stone cooldown in 1.20 and instead introduce durability to warp stones.

- This aligns more with Vanilla gameplay, where the only cooldowns on items are transient cooldowns of a few seconds (e.g. ender pearls)
- It also removes the obscurity in the cooldown being shared across different items, even though durability bars are generally used per-item and not per-item-type
- Unlike resources, time can not be farmed, i.e. the cooldown is a challenge without any means of overcoming it, therefore it is not fun
- Items that use the warp stone in their recipes will likely be changed to use a (new) warp core instead, allowing for a stackable crafting material while still supporting durability on warp stones
- If CraftTweaker/KubeJS have the ability to change item durabilities (not sure atm), there will not be any config option for the durability as pack makers generally have these tweaker mods installed anyways

issues.title: Waystones stop rendering and their names become invalid when used in a large modpack on a dedicated server, when Consistency+ and Universal Graves are present together

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.18.x

### Mod Loader

Fabric

### Mod Loader Version

0.13.3 + FAPI 0.48.0

### Mod Version

10.0.0

### Describe the Issue

Waystones/sharestones stop rendering and their names become "invalid" when I add the mod to my non-public modpack and join a dedicated server with the same modpack. Everything works perfectly fine in single-player. 

I couldn't find out the exact steps to reproduce the issue other than having most of my mods installed along with Waystones, however, I first noticed the issue when I added [Macaw's Roofs](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/macaws-roofs) to my collection. But the mod itself doesn't seem to conflict with Waystones, because I tried loading just Macaw's Roofs + Waystones alone and it worked with no issues on both the server and single-player.

I tried removing mods 1 by 1, trying to figure out which combination of mods causes the conflict, but you pretty much need the entire modpack in order to reproduce the bug.

Mods that definitely don't need to be present for the bug to happen: Bedrockify, Charm, Minecraft Transit Railway, Adorn, Additional Additions. All the client-side mods like Continuity, CITResewn, TieFix (and similar bugfixing mods), MiniHUD (and other HUD mods like WTHIT), Sodium etc.

To get rid of the bug when all the mods are installed, removing only Macaw's Roofs helps, but as I said above, the mods don't conflict with each other on their own.

Another mod that can be removed to fix the bug is Consistency+, in which case Macaw's Roofs and Waystones work fine together along the rest of the modpack, but just like Macaw's Roofs, Consistency+ on its own doesn't cause any issues with Waystones.

I thought that maybe mods that add large amounts of blocks eventually cause the issue, so I only left such mods and tried to replicate the bug to no avail.

I'm honestly just hoping you could help identify what could cause the issue. I understand that my modpack is large and going through all the mod combinations will take an insane amount of time, and I'm not asking for that. However, I hope it would at least be possible to narrow down the mods that could cause this bug at all, so that I don't have to test every single mod combination.

<details>
  <summary>Screenshots</summary>

Placing a waystone down, you can see that the waystone doesn't render at all
![2022-04-09_09 47 32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86702831/162562910-d0b64680-704f-4417-a715-c14172118234.png)
![2022-04-09_09 47 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86702831/162562914-b2255fe9-ad4b-452f-a4a2-0c4b31221daf.png)

Right clicking on the ground next to the waystone with an empty hand, or the waystone itself, renders the bottom half of the waystone
![2022-04-09_09 47 38](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86702831/162562963-f2e866c8-67a1-4570-8e30-4054798c4215.png)

Placing 2 blocks next to it (or even where it's actually supposed to be) makes the whole waystone render, but incorrectly - runes aren't glowing, no particles around the stone
![2022-04-09_09 47 53](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86702831/162563925-cc8ce754-12b6-4c25-a86d-0fe38c167b1c.png)

Right clicking a waystone (even when it's invisible) opens the GUI like normal, but the name is "invalid" and can't be changed
![2022-04-09_09 47 56](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86702831/162563027-e1c5504d-c525-44ac-849e-1c4acead074f.png)

</details>

Other than rendering and showing names, the waystones function as intended, you can teleport between them, scrolls work just fine (including having proper names) etc.

### Logs

https://gist.github.com/Footage2-Amply-Pounce/824043b89fe9caae693367024f79e108

### Do you use any performance-enhancing mods (e.g. OptiFine)?

Sodium + Indium + Sodium Extra, Lithium, LazyDFU, SmoothBoot, Phosphor, Krypton (server optimizations). Removing any/all off these mods doesn't affect the issue.

**Edit:** To add to the performance mods I use: EntityCulling. I noticed another thing that helps waystones to start rendering - leaving the area (and I assume unloading it) and then returning, completely fixes the waystone until you teleport (by any means, not just via waystones) again. However, removing EntityCulling doesn't help and it wouldn't explain why removing Consistency+ and Macaw's Roofs helps.

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.16

### Mod Loader

Forge

### Mod Loader Version

forge-1.16.5-36.2.0

### Mod Version

Waystones_1.16.5-7.6.3

### Describe the Issue

Ok, I have been thrown a lot of "Crash" reports because Chunk Pregen seemed to crash with certain modpacks hard...
After investigating it and having written 5 small rewrites of the logic to adjust for whatever this lag reason was.
We found a crashlog from "Waystones" after CP effectively was set to only save 1 chunk per game tick.

Before waystones was removed Chunk Pregen was able to generate less then 1024 chunks before crashing the game.
(Consistently)
After waystones was removed we were able to generate consistently more then 160k chunks and it only crashed after the pregeneration was done. (different problem)

So clearly  the waystone mod has a issue where it causes a deadlock and causes saving to fail...

And after looking into it. You are initialize the waystone during a save which you should NEVER do.
Never access the world that way. If the instance is not present. Don't try to create it. Just don't save it.

Anyways, this problem is now solved on my side, until this is addressed from your side, i will put a "incompat" warning in so nobody has to deal with these crashes anymore or can at least fix them....

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.17

### Mod Loader

Forge

### Mod Loader Version

37.0.103

### Mod Version

8.1.4+0

### Describe the Issue

When I try to place and rename waystones on the multiplayer server I run, the stones remain <unnamed> and can't be teleported to. Also, when they are placed and destroyed, the number of entries in the waystones list doesn't decrease. The <unnamed> warp points keep stacking up, and you can't warp to any of them. Is there a config setting that I'm missing? Or a mod incompatibility that only shows up in multiplayer?

issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.12

### Mod Loader

Forge

### Mod Loader Version

14.23.5.2855

### Mod Version

Waystones_1.12.2-4.1.0

### Describe the Issue

So i have 230 ish mods, I can upload a list of them or a pack if you want to try to replicate it, I have an imgur with them all on there. I am also running this on a server with a bunch of plugins, but the bug arrived in singleplayer aswell so thats likely not the issue.
I know thats a pain in the ass but im willing to do all the troubleshooting I can on my end if you tell me where to look.

So, anytime the waystones mod opens a gui it "opens" but is invisible, my mouse unlocks, I can interact with it (clicking the warp buttons and i successfully warp to other waystones or typing in the name to name it) but the whole gui is invisible so I have to navigate it blindly / based on memory from previous times ive used the mod. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29662520/138518727-322b7cd1-4853-476d-89cf-2e6f8f4bdec4.png)

Not really easy to show visually because of the nature of the bug, however the picture attached shows what happens. In the picture i had just placed a waystone and am in the gui that is supposed to show a box to let me name the waystone, as i said before i can type the name and hit enter and it all works, but there is no visual meaning my players will have a tough time figuring out what the hell is going on. This isnt the end of the world but when opening the gui to warp between waystones it makes it basically impossible to select the one you want other than through trial and error.

Sorry this is so long, I am willing to do whatever I can on my end just ask. And I hope you can help!
https://imgur.com/a/wkFOuWt
The modlist is in that imgur gallery.
I will upload the pack if you so desire to make your life reproducing easier, just ask!

### Logs

_No response_

### Do you use any performance-enhancing mods (e.g. OptiFine)?

Several:
Optifine
Vanillafix
Patchouli
Performant
Phosfor
and probably some I dont know are performance mods anymore since I made this pack over the past couple weeks.

issues.title: Unloading chunks after teleport?

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

issues.body:
I have no idea if this is a bug or not but I am reporting this just in case it is.

After teleporting, the chunk the waystone is in immediately unloads, which disables anything within its vicinity relying on chunks being loaded. This completely breaks the Simple Storage Networks mod, which rely on the chunk the Network Root is in being loaded. Minecart-portal chunk loaders will also have a 50% chance of breaking depending on if the minecart is in the dimension the waystone is in.

Linked below is the function I think is causing the unloading.
https://github.com/ModdingForBlockheads/Waystones/blob/179a3774b74c8a4fea5ef373a79c78636a25444a/shared/src/java/net/blay09/mods/waystones/core/PlayerWaystoneManager.java#L415

While this can be "fixed" with a chunkloading mod, there are no plans of including one in the pack I am currently using, which is why there is a reliance on chunks being loaded after teleporting away from an area with a waystone.

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Small list of features for Attuned shards to make them a lot better:
1. Stacking of the same coded shards.

It is a bit iritating when you try to make multiple plates all teleport to the same other plate... and each occupies separate slot!
I made six shard all connected to same plate, yet they don't stack together.

2. Attuned Arrows

You can attune arrows inside of plates in order to mark them to set plate.
Shooting entity with arrow teleports it to the plate. Does not work on bosses in order to avoid destruction.
Recipe would require you to put arrows on side slots and single Warp Dust in the middle slot.

3. Modified Plates

Putting different items in side slots modifies properties of plate:
Lever let's you turn the plate on and off. Turned Off plates can't be accessed from other conected to it plates. To turn plate off, you have to charge it with redstone.
Redstone plate of any kind let's you detect any entity being on plate.
Wool will mute the sounds.
Glowstone Dust gives short glowing effect after teleporting into the plate. Could be a nice alarm system!
Glowstone Block would empower the light the plate produces, incase you try to avoid torches as much as you can.
Putting potions allow for one time effect on player after teleportation. Could be a nice trap! Or maybe you want to be immune to fire when going into Nether?

4. Cosmetics and waterlogging

This one is mostly begging for cosmetic options...
We have sandy waystones, where are sandy plates?
Or mossy?

Tho to be fair, I would like few more variants of not just plates, but also waystones, sharestones, portstones...

Also - being able to waterlog those blocks in any way would be really cool. Be it fully or partially.

5. Cheap re-attunning of Shards/Arrows

Putting Attuned shard or shards with single warp dust in any slot let's you re-attune stone to new plate.
Attuned Arrows accept the same price.



I hope you like some of the ideas.

**Versions**

- Forge Version (exact version number): 36.1.31
- Mod Version (exact version number): 7.6.2, Journeymap 5.7.1
- Do you use Sponge, OptiFine or Vivecraft (and which?): none

**Describe the bug**
The Journeymap waypoint integration is not working.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. enable Journeymap integration (inside waystones-client.toml, set "displayWaystonesOnJourneyMap" to "true"
2. In a world, activate an unexplored waystone

**Expected behavior**
As the waystone is activated, a waypoint is supposed to be added to Journeymap.
However, a waypoint is not added to Journeymap.

issues.title: Teleporting with waystones across dimensions causes client side desync, but server still runs even though.

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

issues.body:
**Versions**
- Minecraft Version (exact version number): 1.16.5
- Forge Version (exact version number): 36.1.13 (used to happen on test builds as far back as 36.0.59)
- Mod Version (exact version number): 7.5.1
- Do you use Sponge, OptiFine or Vivecraft (and which?): Optifine G7 (required as G8 crashes Entity Culling for now)

**Describe the bug**
Teleporting with a waystone across dimensions causes a client side desync.  The server still runs and assumes the player has stopped moving.  But the player cannot move at all and cannot see any changes on the server, including particles, entities, tile entities, block changes...though somehow chunks still load in

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install Kaleidio's Battle Pack and make a world with a multiplayer server with the Server Pack.
2. Place a waystone and activate.
3. Place a waystone and activate in some other dimension such as the nether.
4. Try to teleport to the waystone in the other dimension using a waystone.  This will cause the client to load all the chunks and mobs, but all of them are desynced, making them look frozen even though they are not on the server.

**Expected behavior**
Teleporting between waystones in the same dimension works fine. What is it with hopping dimensions that just seems to break?  It also seems specific to dedicated servers...

**Additional context (e.g. Crash Log if it crashed)**
Reproducible if you install Kaleidio's Battle Pack and play on a Kaleidio's Battle Pack Server using the associated server pack.
You can clear out this glitch by leaving the server and rejoining.  You will spawn in the place you teleported to as if no desync ever happened.

issues.body:
I've got to say, I am _LOVING_ the latest update! The sharestones are awesome, and the warp plate is especially cool. I already have ideas for a cool transportation hub on our server.

That said, I'd like to request a couple things that surprised me when they didn't behave the way I expected. On our server, we want to replace all of our global waystones with sharestones, but it appears you cannot use the warp stone to teleport to a SS like you can to a WS. It would be nice if warp stones allowed transportation to either a sharestone _or_ a waystone. Additionally, it would be nice if there was a config to allow waystones to transport you to a sharestone of any color, or for colorless sharestones to allow transport to waystones as well.

issues.body:
**Versions**
- Minecraft Version: 1.16.4
- Forge Version: 35.1.37
- Mod Version: "Waystones 1.16.x v7.3.1"
- Do you use Sponge, OptiFine or Vivecraft (and which?): Optifine HD U G7

**Describe the bug**
In a world created with MC 1.12.2 and Waystones 4.1.0, converting the world to MC 1.16.4 with the versions mentioned above caused all waystones auto-generated in villages to vanish. The surrounding structure remained intact, but the actual waystone was gone. The waystones list in the warp stone UI is empty after conversion.

I also observed a strange failure mode with a world that was originally created with an even older MC version. Here, all waystones were converted into two observer blocks stacked on top of each other. Not really sure what's going on there.

(I'm aware of  #259, but as far as I understand, waystones not being generated in _new_ villages shouldn't cause already existing ones to disappear.)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create world with MC 1.12.2 and Waystones 4.1.0, ensure that waystone generation in villages is turned on
2. Look for any village with a waystone
3. You can activate it or not, doesn't make a difference
4. Switch to MC 1.16.4 with versions as mentioned
5. Waystone is gone

**Expected behavior**
Waystones should not be deleted from the world (and they shouldn't turn into observers either …)

issues.title: [Feature] Player To Not Spawn on Top of Waystone

labels.name: Support
labels.description: Questions and other requests for help

type.name: Support
type.description: Questions and other requests for help

issues.body:
Minecraft 1.16.4
Forge 35.1.37
Waystones 7.3.1

Please make it so players do not teleport directly on top of the waystone block. 

**Issue:**
Players get teleported directly on top of the waystone. It is awkward, immersion breaking, and limiting (we have to build ceilings higher than what we want - otherwise the player suffocates)

**Proposal:**
Players teleport into a 3x3 area around the waystone (excluding the waystone's position):

[  ] [  ] [  ]
[  ] [X] [  ]
[  ] [  ] [  ]

**Breakdown:**
Each waystone has an acceptedTeleportPoints array which contains eight teleportPointObjects.
Each teleportPointObject (the eight surrounding blocks around the waystone) has four properties:
 1) x coordinate
 2) y coordinate
 3) z coordinate
 2) blocktype

Two examples of  TeleportPoint objects:
{
    x: -100
    y: 56
    z:  280
    blocktype: minecraft:air
    isValid: true
}

{
    x: -101
    y: 56
    z:  281
    blocktype: minecraft:stone
    isValid: false
}

Example of waystone's acceptedTeleportPoints array: [{}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {}]

The TeleportPoint objects are updated/populated on waystone placement.
 
 
**Function to select which point to teleport to with validation to prevent the player from sufficating in a wall:**
// on player selecting a waystone to teleport to..
// if all 8 blocks' isValid values are false, then player cannot teleport there - mark the 
    waystone name in red, or make it unselectable, or tell the player that waystone is 
    unavailable or something.
// randomly select one of teleportPointObjects in the AcceptedTeleportPoints array
  // if that object's isValid value is true..
    // player will be teleported to that xyz coordinate
  // else randomly select another teleportPointObject 
 

**Option For Better Performance:**
Issue:
players can update blocks around the waystone after it has been placed (which means the objects in the AcceptedTeleportPoints array needs to be updated to match)

When/how often to update TeleportPoint objects?
To not have the block-validation-check run all the time, only update the array when the player tries to teleport to that waystone.


**Note:**
If you have a more concise/better coding solution, please feel free to do it your own way. I just wanted to share my thoughts and how I would probably go about doing this.

### Overview

I tried to build this mod from source. It would not build, and after making some adjustments to force it to build, it would not run.

The modifications I wanted to make to the mod are documented in issue #312 ; however, the bug I'm reporting here occurs even without such modifications, with exactly the same presentation.

Please advise on how to get this build to work. Am I doing something wrong here?

### Platform

**OS**: Debian Buster amd64
**Gradle**: 4.9 (via gradlew)
**Java**: OpenJDK 11
**Minecraft**: 1.16.3
**Forge**: 34.1.35

### Steps to reproduce build failure

    git clone https://github.com/blay09/Waystones
    cd Waystones
    git branch # shows 1.16.x
    ./gradlew build --stacktrace

Result:

    FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.

    * Where:
    Build file '/home/jaime/Builds/Waystones/build.gradle' line: 98

    * What went wrong:
    A problem occurred evaluating root project 'Waystones'.
    > /home/jaime/.gradle/daemon/4.9/run/obfmods

    * Try:
    Run with --info or --debug option to get more log output. Run with --scan to get full insights.

    * Exception is:
    org.gradle.api.GradleScriptException: A problem occurred evaluating root project 'Waystones'.
        at org.gradle.groovy.scripts.internal.DefaultScriptRunnerFactory$ScriptRunnerImpl.run(DefaultScriptRunnerFactory.java:92)
        at org.gradle.configuration.DefaultScriptPluginFactory$ScriptPluginImpl$2.run(DefaultScriptPluginFactory.java:204)
        [...]
        at org.gradle.internal.concurrent.ThreadFactoryImpl$ManagedThreadRunnable.run(ThreadFactoryImpl.java:55)
    Caused by: java.io.FileNotFoundException: /home/jaime/.gradle/daemon/4.9/run/obfmods
        at build_5tfaqiqvds7g6qw2h7simwwhj$_run_closure4.doCall(/home/jaime/Builds/Waystones/build.gradle:98)
        at java.base/jdk.internal.reflect.NativeMethodAccessorImpl.invoke0(Native Method)
        [...]
        at org.gradle.groovy.scripts.internal.DefaultScriptRunnerFactory$ScriptRunnerImpl.run(DefaultScriptRunnerFactory.java:90)
        ... 99 more

Part of build.gradle that causes this error, starting at line 89 as per the error message:

    def obfModsDir = new File("run/obfmods")
    obfModsDir.eachFile { file ->
        def parts = file.name.split('-', 2)
        def dep = "ignored:" + parts[0] + ":" + parts[1].replace(".jar", "");
        runtimeOnly fg.deobf(dep)
    }

Bizarrely, this error occurs even if the file run/obfmods exists (in my case /home/jaime/.gradle/daemon/4.9/run/obfmods). Having it be a directory also does not help.

### Steps to reproduce runtime failure

I tried commenting out the offending code concerning obfModsDir:

    /*def obfModsDir = new File("run/obfmods")
    obfModsDir.eachFile { file ->
        def parts = file.name.split('-', 2)
        def dep = "ignored:" + parts[0] + ":" + parts[1].replace(".jar", "");
        runtimeOnly fg.deobf(dep)

labels.description: New features or improvements to existing features

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Hello, first of all I want to say that nothing of this is a request for you to implement it.
I would either code this myself as an addon mod if possible, or open a PR.

I've had this idea for a specific feature and wanted you to tell me what you think about it and whether or not I should implement it as a separate addon mod or open a PR to this repo.

The core idea is waystones being able to be grouped, resulting in a set of mechanics.
A waystone group would be completely defined via datapacks.
`/data/namespace/waystone/groups/groupname.json`

The waystone json file would contain the following information
- Which other waystone groups would be accessible by this.
- Whether the group is accessible by non-grouped waystones
- A list of conditions which have to be fulfilled to travel to a waystone in this group
- A list of predicates to automatically assign this group to a waystone if any matches

Conditions could be anything from the players having a certain level to him carrying a specific item.
Predicates would auto-assign a waystone to a group if it was placed in a specific dimension or a specific height, etc

```
{
    "display_name": "The End",
    "canAccess": [
        "namespace:some_group",
        "namespace:other_group"
    ],
    "private": true,
    "conditions": [
        {
            "type": "has_item",
            "item": "minecraft:diamond",
            "negate": true
        }
    ],
    "predicates": [
        {
            "type": "dimension",
            "dimension": "minecraft:the_end"
        }
    ]
}
```

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

I tested this with a waystone at spawn with and without path and had the same issue, although I had to teleport a distance away and then back again in order to actually trigger it.

This is the waypoint set up at the other player's location:

![](https://thumbs.gfycat.com/GrizzledSimilarEstuarinecrocodile-size_restricted.gif)

And here is the waypoint set up at spawn:

![](https://thumbs.gfycat.com/TiredSoulfulBlackrussianterrier-size_restricted.gif)

Another player teleported to the one at spawn in front of me and had a few visual glitches. They described it as: "It started jittering a bit like I was getting stuck, but I was able to jump out"

I think the waystone name config could be improved, by adding a few more options. To not clutter the main mod's config, it could generate in it's own file.

A few suggestions:
- Generate the list of default names, so users can edit them freely. (Allows people to remove or alter any they want, and aren't forced to have their custom names just generate once before going into default)

- Allow editing of the naming conventions, including adding new ones (so not every one is "[Name Here] [Biome here]")

- Allow names and naming conventions to be linked to the biome the waystone is in, instead of just attaching the biome name to the end (So a name like "Town of Plank Hills" only occurs in Extreme Hills)

I feel like this system would help modpack authors to better alter waystones to fit their theme, and so I could make a bunch of random references to Zelda 2 without them generating all as the first towns you find, regardless of biome.

issues.title: [CRASH] getDurabilityForDisplay assumes player is never null

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: Crash
labels.description: Bugs that cause the game to crash

issues.body:
At clientside startup it's possible for Forge to trigger ForgeEventFactory.onItemTooltip with NULL for the player (as indicated w/the @nullable annotation). If this occurs, this crash can happen (a specific stack is clipped below):

```
at net.blay09.mods.waystones.PlayerWaystoneHelper.getWaystonesTag(PlayerWaystoneHelper.java:19)
	at net.blay09.mods.waystones.PlayerWaystoneHelper.getLastWarpStoneUse(PlayerWaystoneHelper.java:63)
	at net.blay09.mods.waystones.item.ItemWarpStone.getDurabilityForDisplay(ItemWarpStone.java:99)
	at net.blay09.mods.waystones.item.ItemWarpStone.showDurabilityBar(ItemWarpStone.java:93)
	at org.jwaresoftware.mcmods.smarthoppers.runtime.TooltipEnricher.onItemTooltip(TooltipEnricher.java:87)
	at net.minecraftforge.fml.common.eventhandler.ASMEventHandler_678_TooltipEnricher_onItemTooltip_ItemTooltipEvent.invoke(.dynamic)
	at net.minecraftforge.fml.common.eventhandler.ASMEventHandler.invoke(ASMEventHandler.java:90)
	at net.minecraftforge.fml.common.eventhandler.EventBus.post(EventBus.java:182)
	at net.minecraftforge.event.ForgeEventFactory.onItemTooltip(ForgeEventFactory.java:325)
	at net.minecraft.item.ItemStack.func_82840_a(ItemStack.java:889)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.lambda$populateSearchTreeManager$1(Minecraft.java:575)
	at net.minecraft.client.util.SearchTree.func_194042_b(SourceFile:49)
	at net.minecraft.client.util.SearchTree.func_194043_a(SourceFile:44)
```

The original call is populating the client-side search index on startup. The TooltipEnricher mod calls getDurability with the ItemStack it's provided (no EntityPlayer from here...but ItemWarpStone is mapping into Minecraft.player which is null). Also appparently the Item durability methods are not only client-side methods (although I also thought they were...doesn't help in this case anyways as it's from client side the crash is triggered)

**Version details:**
```
| UCH   | waystones   | 4.0.43    | Waystones_1.12.2-4.0.43.jar
forge-1.12.2-14.23.4.2705-universal.jar
```

issues.title: [enhancement]  Worldgen waystones are much to common.

labels.name: Support
labels.description: Questions and other requests for help

type.name: Support
type.description: Questions and other requests for help

issues.body:
Having waystones produced in worldgen is a good idea, but as implemented, they're way too common.

Short of leaving them disabled entirely, the config file offers a minimum frequency of 1 in 10,000 blocks.  That's a square 100 blocks on a side, which leaves them fairly well littering the landscape -- to the point that the only reason to make your own waystone would be to pick the name.  (About that -- the person who activates it really should get to pick the name.)

My advice would be first, to change that frequency value to _chunks_, and second, to also add a minimum distance value.  I also advise adding a separate enable/disable entry in the config file; this will let you supply default values, say 1 per 1000 chunks with a minimum distance of 300 blocks.  (Those values may still be a bit low.)
